archive/stream#

Archives read or written one member at a time.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let tar = TarReading(origin: file.binary(), limits: limits);
defer tar.close();
loop {
    last if tar.finished();
    let entry = tar.entry();
    …
}

Description#

Archives read or written one member at a time.

ReadingArchive gives members until finished(); WritingArchive takes them and then finish() writes the archive's end. Both are resources: close them.

object ArchiveReading#

object ArchiveReading does ReadingArchive, Closing

Shared lifecycle adapter over an explicit synchronous one-entry operation. Construction does not invoke it. Each active entry() invokes it exactly once, retains no returned member and does not prefetch. The operation must enforce ArchiveLimits BEFORE materializing payload; this adapter cannot retroactively bound returned data. Format errors and actual allocation bounds belong to the operation/concrete reader. Captured dependencies follow normal closure lifetime. Owns only status: empty=active, byte 1=normal EOF, byte 2=processing failure.

let stream = ArchiveReading(() is ArchiveEntry { source.entry(); });
let member = stream.entry(); // may throw EndOfArchive
stream.close();             // does not close source

object ArchiveWriting#

object ArchiveWriting does WritingArchive, Closing

Shared writer lifecycle. The supplied write/finish operations perform all format work and documented flushing. They receive the exact entry once; the adapter neither inspects members nor independently flushes/closes a sink. Constructor only binds operations and private state. A failed write or finish poisons the stream, including an EndOfArchive raised by a writer operation. Destructor/close never invoke either operation or synthesize a terminator.
